name: Willow Inference Server (WIS)
description: toverainc's self-hosted, GPU-optimized inference server for speech (Whisper ASR) and TTS, and the backend for the Willow ESP32 voice-assistant hardware. Exposes REST, WebSocket, and WebRTC transports on port 19000 with an interactive Swagger UI at /api/docs and a WebRTC demo client at /rtc. No built-in authentication by default. The served Swagger UI and demo pages make it partially Shodan http.html-visible.
auth_notes: No default authentication. WIS serves its REST API, interactive docs (/api/docs), Willow integration endpoint (/api/willow), and a WebRTC demo client (/rtc) on port 19000 (HTTPS, typically self-signed) with no credential enforcement out of the box. The Swagger UI at /api/docs renders endpoint names and the WIS identity into served HTML, so basic fingerprinting works via Shodan http.html; the WebRTC/WebSocket audio transports themselves are wire-only. TLS uses an operator-generated (often self-signed) cert, so wss/https is on but identity is unverified.

shodan_dorks.rationale: Project name rendered in the served Swagger UI / demo client HTML on the default 19000 port; high signal
The /api/willow integration path is near-unique to WIS and appears in the /api/docs Swagger body; distinguishes it from generic FastAPI/whisper servers
Willow name plus the WebRTC demo-client path /rtc in the same document is very high precision and low volume
WIS version disclosure in the Swagger info block or /api docs; use for version-targeted enumeration

known_vulns: No built-in auth — unauthenticated POST /api/asr and /api/tts accept arbitrary audio/text at operator GPU cost
Swagger UI /api/docs enabled by default — full API schema disclosure aids automated enumeration
Self-signed TLS provides encryption but no identity assurance — MITM-able, no client authentication
GPU compute theft — Whisper large-v2 ASR + TTS on CUDA with no rate limiting; automatable abuse
Audio PII exfiltration — voice-assistant command audio and dictations processed with no consent or audit logging
WebRTC/WebSocket transports exposed unauthenticated; the /rtc demo client hands an attacker a ready-made streaming interface
Early/rapidly-advancing codebase — hardening and stable release surface are immature
risk_notes: Primary attack vectors: (1) Compute theft — an open 19000 endpoint is free GPU ASR+TTS, driveable via the shipped Swagger UI and /rtc client. (2) Voice-assistant audio exfiltration — WIS backs the Willow ESP32 hardware, so exposed instances often carry home/office command audio (highly sensitive) processed with no auth or logging. (3) MITM via self-signed TLS — the cert authenticates nothing on the WebRTC/REST transports. (4) Schema-driven enumeration — /api/docs discloses every endpoint and parameter shape. (5) The /rtc WebRTC demo gives an attacker a turnkey real-time speech pipe into the operator's GPU.
deployment_notes: Self-hosted on CUDA GPU hosts (CPU fallback supported). Default HTTPS bind on port 19000 (typically self-signed cert). Serves REST (/api/asr, /api/tts, /api/willow), a Swagger UI at /api/docs (Shodan http.html-visible), and a WebRTC demo client at /rtc; the real-time audio rides WebRTC/WebSocket (wire-only). Ready-to-deploy Docker containers were promised for the 1.0 release; earlier versions build from source. Primary role is the backend for the Willow open-source voice-assistant hardware (toverainc/willow), so exposed instances frequently serve real household/office voice-command traffic. No auth by default; project self-describes as very early and advancing rapidly. Basic host discovery via the served Swagger UI; deep transport work needs active WebRTC probing.
